result.title: MemCredit: From Relevance to Utility for Decision-Time Memory in Long-Horizon Web Agents
result.summary: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly operate over long Web interaction histories, making memory management critical for reliable and efficient decision making. Existing methods primarily optimize storage, retrieval, or compression, but the memories most semantically relevant to the current state are not necessarily those that most improve the agent's action. We introduce MemCredit, a decision-centric memory framework that shifts memory selection from semantic relevance to decision utility. MemCredit estimates the state-, reference-context-, and policy-conditional marginal contribution of individual memories through controlled counterfactual interventions, and distills these intervention-derived credits into a lightweight utility estimator. At inference time, semantic relevance is used only for high-recall candidate generation, while predicted utility arbitrates which memories are retained under a fixed token budget, without modifying the underlying agent policy or requiring additional environment interaction. We evaluate MemCredit on ALFWorld and WebShop against representative memory baselines. On ALFWorld, MemCredit achieves 86.57 SR@50 under a 500-token historical-memory budget, compared with 65.67% for BM25 retrieval. Counterfactual analysis further shows that memory utility is sparse, strongly state dependent, and poorly captured by semantic relevance. These results suggest that decision utility provides a more effective principle than relevance alone for long-horizon agent memory management.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 MemCredit，把长程 Web agent 的记忆选择从语义相关性改为决策效用：用受控反事实干预估计单条记忆对当前状态的边际贡献，并蒸馏成轻量效用估计器，推理时先高召回召候选、再按预测效用和固定 token 预算筛选记忆。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「反事实边际贡献→效用估计器→预算内筛选」的流程可供核查 LVR 中视觉或 latent 证据筛选与贡献分配问题，但该工作面向纯文本交互记忆、未涉及视觉状态，属方法线索而非主线研究。
